query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a nozzle-specific spray distance optimized for higher particle velocity (around 300–350 mm) with the HVAF-i7 torch will overcome the current thickness limitation while maintaining the desired coating properties.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with 15–45 μm particle size as used in previous HVAF-M3 depositions.
generation.intervention: Adjust the processing parameter by setting the HVAF-i7 nozzle stand‐off distance to approximately 300–350 mm (the value that yielded higher particle velocity and deposition efficiency in MCrAlY studies on the M3 system) instead of the default setting.
generation.conditions: Deposition should be performed using the HVAF-i7 torch under otherwise identical settings (feedstock composition, particle size, and atmosphere) with the adjusted spray distance. The service condition remains high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
generation.structural_mediator: An increase in particle velocity resulting in a higher in-flight kinetic energy of the particles that promotes a greater deposition rate and improved bonding efficiency.
generation.mechanism: Shortening the spray distance to the optimal 300–350 mm increases the velocity of the particles upon impact, thereby enhancing deposition efficiency and overcoming the growth limitation on coating thickness, while still preserving acceptable adhesion and low as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A thicker bond coat compared to the baseline deposition using the standard HVAF-i7 parameters (with 15–45 μm feedstock), while retaining acceptable quality in terms of coating integrity and oxidation level.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced with the HVAF-i7 torch using a 15–45 μm feedstock at the default spray distance, which showed acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: The intervention should not compromise the overall coating integrity, adhesion, and oxidation resistance, especially within constrained geometries (internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under high-temperature service conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the thickness increase and any minor changes in oxidation levels are uncertain, although the expectation is a noticeable improvement consistent with previous studies on the M3 system.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled deposition experiment using the HVAF-i7 torch with two sets of spray distances: one at the default setting and one adjusted to 300–350 mm. Use the same FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock (15–45 μm) and deposit coatings on substrates featuring internal diameters as small as 120 mm. Evaluate the coatings after deposition for thickness, adherence, as-sprayed oxidation levels, and overall quality.
measurements: Coating thickness (using cross-sectional microscopy or profilometry)
Oxide content (using X-ray diffraction or surface analysis techniques)
Microstructural integrity (via SEM or similar imaging)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings deposited with the adjusted spray distance do not show a statistically significant increase in thickness relative to those deposited with the default parameters, or if any deterioration in coating integrity, adhesion, or oxidation resistance is observed, then the hypothesis would be falsified.
